environment.mode: Electron headless with explicit 1280×860 renderer viewport, isolated userData; native open/save dialogs stubbed only for deterministic file selection

limitations: Measured on one Linux host only. Windows and macOS are unmeasured.
Headless requestAnimationFrame is a rendering scheduling proxy, not physical monitor presentation latency.
Playwright keyboard.insertText dispatches committed Unicode text; it does not exercise a real Chinese IME.
The native file picker is replaced with an immediate selection. Human picker time is excluded.
Initial editor launch is warmed before opening the long document. Open timing is document-open-to-editable, not application cold launch.

coldStartup.method: Node monotonic time immediately before Playwright Electron launch → first renderer reports moye.ready; includes automation process/debugger/viewport setup and font preload, excludes human interaction.

viewport.note: Per-input scroll/caret samples detect large resets. This is not proof that no intermediate display frame ever flickered.

keyboardEndToEnd.method: Node performance.now → await Playwright keyboard.insertText(one committed Unicode character) → renderer next requestAnimationFrame callback and IPC response
keyboardEndToEnd.interpretation: Conservative automation command roundtrip diagnostic, including IPC and potentially an additional frame; this is not physical input-to-display latency.

keyboardEventToFrame.method: Renderer capture of real Playwright-dispatched beforeinput (fallback input) → next requestAnimationFrame; excludes command/response IPC outside the renderer

pageInsertToFrame.method: Renderer performance.now → document.execCommand(insertText, one character) → next requestAnimationFrame; excludes Playwright input IPC

fullDocumentGetValue.note: Eight isolated calls after the input test; useful attribution, not an independent input latency measurement.

warmKeyboardDiagnostic.note: Same characters entered a second time, after initial glyph/font use. This diagnostic does not replace or relax the first-use input acceptance gates.

recommendations: Profile the input handler on the same fixture. Avoid serializing and reparsing the complete document synchronously for every input event.
Keep immediate DOM editing responsive while batching noncritical word count, outline and recovery serialization work.
Remeasure on Windows/macOS and target user hardware before claiming cross-platform performance acceptance.
